transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01
Start: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Nadia Park, Ethan Li, Priya Rao, Marcus Nguyen, Olivia Chen, Samir Patel

Summary:
Quick workshop to align on ship integrity (safety circuit) for upcoming service release. Cover dependency matrix, runtime fallback knobs, canary acceptance criteria, and a 12-hour stress/chaos window. Identify owners and short timeline for a dry-run next week.

Topics covered:
- dependency mapping and critical path libraries
- canary acceptance and rollback criteria
- runtime safe-mode toggles and observed perf delta
- long-window load test + KV/prefix cache behaviour
- incident handoff and oncall choreography

Transcript body:
[00:00] Nadia: alright hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. our goal today is narrow — walk through what we need to ship the safety circuit for the new inference routing, and make sure we have owners for the canary and the long-window run.
[00:18] Ethan: yep, started the doc in the shared drive, added the initial hypothesis about where latency spikes show up during prefix-heavy workloads. i can share the spreadsheet after.
[00:25] Priya: ok cool. quick thing — the dependency map I'm building shows two native libraries that have pathologic OOMs under sustained 1k-concurrency. one is the matrix-kernel pack and the other is an allocator shim from the 3rd party lib we still vendor.
[00:40] Marcus: is that the same allocator that we saw mis-report memory on the 40B runs last quarter?
[00:44] Priya: yeah, likely the same. in the repro it's subtle; under continuous KV cache refill the working set grows and then sam-el — sorry SAML — the process reports small heap but OOMs. transcription note: the allocator misreports, it confuses our eviction heuristics.
[01:02] Olivia: we should add that as a must-fail case in canary tests. if OOMs appear, it's a showstopper. even if latency is ok for a bit.
[01:10] Samir: from product side, the acceptance bar for canary is: no >=95th percentile spike above 150ms for prompt results, no silent failures, and clear rollback path within 15 minutes. is that realistic?
[01:24] Ethan: the 150ms p95 is tight for some workloads, but with prefix caching and batching we can generally hit it on dedicated infra. on hosted we might need a fallback model variant to keep latency SLOs.
[01:37] Marcus: that's where the runtime safe-mode comes in — we have three toggles: quantized fallback, shorter KV retention, and immediate batch cutoff. I can add them behind feature flags. we should document expected token-level cost delta for each.
[01:51] Priya: please also surface which flags are hot-switchable vs require restart. that affects canary rollback time.
[01:58] Marcus: good point — quantized fallback and batch cutoff are hot, KV retention change needs restart.
[02:06] Nadia: ok mark KV retention as restart-only. that means our rollback window expands if we ever hit that path.
[02:12] (short overlap) Ethan: and we need a runbook entry for how oncall toggles flags — who has rights, and an escalation path to infra for restarts.
[02:20] Nadia: exactly. Olivia, can you own the runbook checklist for canary toggles?
[02:24] Olivia: yes, I'll draft it. will include the exact commands and API endpoints for toggling the flags in dedicated and private deploys.
[02:31] Samir: timeline check — ship target is next Friday launch window, we should dry-run at least two days before.
[02:38] Nadia: that leaves us a week, which is tight. Priya, how long to finish the dependency matrix?
[02:42] Priya: i can finish the matrix and call out restart vs hot flags by monday EOD — 2027-09-06.
[02:48] Marcus: i'll prioritize the runtime toggles doc this Friday and share a PR in #runtime.
[02:53] Ethan: about the 12-hour chaos run — i'm proposing we run a full-day test with synthetic prefixes and KV prefill to exercise cache eviction. we saw small steady-state leaks in staging, haven't reproduced in a 12h window.
[03:05] Olivia: what tooling will you use? flakiness makes the transcript, sorry — flakiness makes the test noisy.
[03:10] Ethan: i plan to use our load harness + a chaos shim to kill one worker every 30 minutes, and a KV prefill step at start. i'll attach the harness config to the ticket.
[03:19] Priya: add the matrix-kernel diagnostic flag to collect heap stats every 30s; we need fine-grained memory traces, not just oom logs.
[03:26] Marcus: watch out for kernel instrumentation overhead — collecting at 30s could change behavior. maybe do 60s unless we need higher fidelity for the repro.
[03:33] Priya: noted, we'll start at 60s and bump if necessary.
[03:36] (crosstalk) Nadia: let’s keep iteration fast — capture failures, escalate, and do a rollback rehearsal.
[03:43] Samir: rehearsal: who will own the rollback rehearsal and play the oncall responder?
[03:48] Ethan: i'll be primary responder, Marcus will handle runtime changes, Priya infra restarts, Olivia will validate canary health checks and runbook steps.
[03:56] Nadia: perfect. put that in the invite for the dry-run.
[03:59] Olivia: quick QA ask — canary acceptance should include sanity checks for outputs. we must ensure reranked prompts still stable — not just latency.
[04:07] Marcus: yeah add a lightweight eval set that runs against canary; if BLEU / similarity drops beyond threshold we abort.
[04:14] Samir: specify thresholds — maybe automated eval tolerances: no more than 2% drop in quality metrics across the set, otherwise auto-abort.
[04:23] Nadia: add that to acceptance criteria doc.
[04:27] Ethan: one more ops note: we need audit logging of who toggles flags. SSO/SAML logs exist but we should mirror toggles in the deployment audit stream for incident review.
[04:38] Priya: yep, will add a logging hook to the feature flag service; it's a small change.
[04:43] Marcus: also capturing token-level cost delta from toggles — we should measure cost per 1k tokens for each safe-mode and include that on the console.
[04:51] Nadia: consolidate that as part of the rollout doc — expected latency and cost deltas, and a binary rollback path.
[04:57] (brief silence while people type)
[05:05] Ethan: about postmortem fragments — if we see repeated partial regressions we should open a P1 fragment and not wait for full outage. small fragments help root cause faster.
[05:15] Samir: agree. add a triage owner for fragment handling.
[05:19] Olivia: i'll be the triage owner during the dry-run window.
[05:22] Nadia: great. last quick item: can someone confirm private deployment implications? KMS/HSM keys, onprem network egress, any blocking security reviews?
[05:33] Priya: security has signalled one more ACC review for HSM rotation, but not blocking. we'll need a short IMM with security to confirm canary controls for private.
[05:41] Nadia: ok i'll book 30 min with security on Tuesday.
[05:44] (overlap) Marcus: also flag that some private customers run older quant kernels; we need a compatibility matrix.
[05:51] Priya: adding that to the dependency map.
[05:54] Nadia: ok let's recap owners and dates.
[05:57] (recap) Nadia: Priya — dependency matrix and restart vs hot flags by 2027-09-06.
[06:03] Nadia: Marcus — runtime safe-mode flags doc and expected perf/cost delta by 2027-09-03.
[06:08] Nadia: Ethan — schedule and run 12-hour chaos with KV prefill and worker kills, results by 2027-09-08.
[06:13] Nadia: Olivia — canary checklist and sanity evals by 2027-09-04, triage on dry-run.
[06:18] Nadia: Samir — sign off acceptance thresholds and communicate to stakeholders by 2027-09-02.
[06:22] (small confirmations)
[06:25] Nadia: any final blockers?
[06:27] Ethan: none from me.
[06:28] Priya: none, will get started.
[06:30] Marcus: i'll post the PR.
[06:32] Olivia: will start the checklist template.
[06:34] Nadia: great. i'll send the calendar invite for the dry-run and the security sync. thanks everyone.
[06:38] (meeting ends)
